data.description: Elevation allows elements to be lifted from the background. It can be defined by applying drop shadows or other visual cues, such as color and borders

shadows.description: Elevation using shadows reflects a spatial relationship by indicating separation from the background or allowing content to be scrolled under another element. The system uses a multi-layered shadow approach with four distinct levels (0-300) defined as CSS custom properties.

levels.name: Tatami Shadow 0
levels.description: Zero elevation / no shadow - 0px offset, 0px blur, transparent black. Used as a reset or base state.

levels.name: Tatami Shadow 100
levels.description: Subtle elevation with two layers: 0px 0.7px 1.462px at 1.6% opacity and 0px 3px 9px at 3.1% opacity. Light lift effect.

levels.name: Tatami Shadow 200
levels.description: Medium elevation with four layers ranging from 0.175px to 4px vertical offset, with blur values from 1px to 18px. Opacity ranges from 1.2% to 4%.

levels.name: Tatami Shadow 300
levels.description: Maximum elevation with six layers from 0.667px to 36px vertical offset, blur values from 3.5px to 89px. Creates deep, prominent shadow for highest z-index elements.

levels.name: Tw Ring Offset Shadow
levels.description: Tailwind utility ring offset shadow - transparent placeholder shadow used for focus ring styling.
